clue.text: Singer still performing, gaining money through discs

parts.note: still means calm and tranquil, so placid

indicators.note: the inner group passes right through between the two discs, so they sit either side of it

parts.note: two discs are two round letters O

indicators.note: the word for performing takes in the money letter, as if gaining it

parts.note: performing a task is doing it

explanation.surface: A tenor who still sings is earning plenty from his records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' puts M inside DOING to make DOMING; 'through' has that run between the two O discs.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Spanish operatic tenor, one of the Three Tenors, is a singer.

clue.text: Cleanse odd bits leaving very ropy thing?

indicators.note: the letters in the odd positions of the word cleanse go, keeping the even ones

parts.note: so, as in 'so tired', means very

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrub something until its stray scraps leave it rather stringy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of CLEANSE leaves LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noose is made of rope, so it is playfully a 'ropy' item.

clue.text: Authorised one to disturb Olympics chief (Viscount perhaps)

indicators.note: the pieces break into the chief's name, disturbing it from inside

parts.note: Sebastian Coe chaired the London 2012 Olympics organisers and was made a peer
OK means approved or authorised
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with permission is sent to upset Lord Coe, the Olympic boss who is a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Coe is in fact a life peer, so 'Viscount' feels like his title; it is a brand of British mint biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscount is a British brand of chocolate biscuit, an example of a biscuit, which Americans call this.

clue.text: State benefit restricts smart chap, returning time after time for cheese

indicators.note: the benefit word holds the other letters within it, restricting them

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

indicators.note: one time letter is placed after the other
the chap's name comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all, so Alec is the smart chap
T again for time
T again for time

explanation.surface: A smart fellow on benefits keeps coming back for cheese, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart chap' rests on the phrase smart alec, a know-all; 'returning' turns his name round, and 'restricts' has the dole hold it with the two times.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolcelatte is a soft, creamy Italian blue cheese, a type of cheese.

clue.text: Second-in-command not recording tax

indicators.note: not signals that the recording letters are left out

parts.note: a deputy is the second in command
an EP, an extended-play record, is a recording

explanation.surface: The deputy leader declines to put any tax on record.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a tax, as on imported goods or alcohol.

clue.text: Top artists from West disrobe without pressure

parts.note: Mae West, the American actress, so her first name

indicators.note: without means the pressure letter is dropped

parts.note: to strip is to disrobe
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Leading painters from the western world undress without being pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from West' looks like a direction; West is the actress Mae West, giving MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri, plural of maestro, are masters of an art, especially great musicians.

clue.text: Fish net repeatedly tangled with oar

indicators.note: tangled says the letters of the nets and oar are knotted into a new order
repeatedly means the word net is used twice

parts.note: the word net, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishing net keeps getting snarled up with an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: The neon tetra is a small, brightly striped tropical aquarium fish.

clue.text: Anti-royalist organ occupies old college storage space satisfactorily

indicators.note: the organ sits inside, occupying, the old college letters

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ
ROM, read-only memory, is computer storage
well means satisfactorily

explanation.surface: A church organ is crammed into storage at an old college, quite satisfactorily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music, fitting college and storage; it is the bodily one.
explanation.definitionFit: He led Parliament's side against Charles I and ruled England as Lord Protector after the king's execution.

clue.text: Part of body cold sitting in ground seat somewhere near 'arrow

indicators.note: the cold word sits inside the rearranged seat
ground, as in ground down or crushed, says the letters of seat are broken up

parts.note: the word seat, taken as written
a chill is a cold
Hendon is a district near Harrow in north-west London; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'arrow signals, it is 'endon

explanation.surface: A bit of the body feels cold sitting on a seat on the ground somewhere near Harrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal, not soil. Hendon and Harrow are London suburbs; the dropped H of 'arrow means Hendon loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendon joining calf muscle to heel bone is a part of the body.

clue.text: Players keep fuelled regularly by knocking back huge meal

indicators.note: the players hold the other letters inside, keeping them

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show

indicators.note: knocking back means the huge abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for huge

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of fuelled

explanation.surface: The actors keep well fed by downing an enormous dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like drinking; it is the reversal signal, and 'regularly' picks every other letter of fuelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a rich French bean and meat stew, a hearty and filling dish.

clue.text: Adverse rocks to cross — see, that could be a health hazard

definitions.text: that could be a health hazard

indicators.note: read as ad-verse, against the verse, so the whole is turned backwards
the frozen word goes across the see word, holding it inside

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: Treacherous ice to walk across: look, it could be dangerous to your health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adverse' looks like an adjective for rocks; it reverses ILOCE, the ice word round LO.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterium causes food poisoning, so it could be a danger to health.

clue.text: Spread lies after wedding vow — it's what churchgoers might do

indicators.note: the rearranged lies come after the vow

parts.note: I do is the vow said at a wedding

indicators.note: spread here means the letters of lies are spread out into another arrangement

explanation.surface: After the wedding vows, gossip spreads lies, which is what churchgoers might do.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchgoers worship, and to worship or revere is the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Woman possesses rubbish bust?

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the rubbish inside it

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A woman owns a cheap, worthless bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a woman's chest or a breakdown; it is the sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders, an example of a carved figure, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Links traveller with common sense and formal clothing

parts.note: a car is something that travels
nous is British slang for common sense
a tie is worn with formal clothing; white tie is formal dress

explanation.surface: A traveller with practical sense in a smart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Links' looks like a connecting word; it is a seaside golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are seaside golf courses, and this one in Scotland has hosted the Open Championship.

clue.text: Left foot kicks a branch

indicators.note: kicks, as in kicking a habit, means giving up the letter a

parts.note: an iamb is a metrical foot in poetry

explanation.surface: A left-footer kicks a fallen branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' suggests the body; it is the poetic foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of a tree is a large branch.

clue.text: Ex-footballer with Rooney's number entering code (Northern)

indicators.note: the shirt number goes into the code

parts.note: Morse is the dot-and-dash code
Wayne Rooney wore the number ten shirt for England and Manchester United

explanation.surface: A former footballer with Rooney's shirt number joins a northern club's code.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Mortensen was an England forward who scored a hat-trick in the 1953 FA Cup final for Blackpool.

clue.text: Rich sort of celebrity, in charge, resigned

parts.note: rich food is fatty, and fat means rich or lavish
an A-list celebrity is a top-tier one

explanation.surface: A wealthy star who was running things has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resigned' suggests quitting a post; it means accepting one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resigned to something means accepting that it is inevitable, the outlook of a believer in fate.

clue.text: Republican writer can enter court, a London landmark

indicators.note: the three pieces go into the court word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the papal court
a pen is a writing instrument
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A Republican author is able to come into court at a famous London spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb; it is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serpentine is the curving lake in Hyde Park, a famous London sight.

clue.text: Learned sport in correct dress, at centre

indicators.note: the sport goes inside the correcting word

parts.note: to edit a text is to correct it
RU is rugby union, a sport

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word dress is taken

explanation.surface: A scholar's sport is to tidy up his dress at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' could be a past tense; it is the adjective, scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, said of a person, means well-read and scholarly, a synonym.

clue.text: Panel beginning to decry song and dance

indicators.note: the opening letter of decry is used

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: A judging panel begins to condemn a song-and-dance act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panel' looks like a judging panel; it is a strip of wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower panel of an interior wall, often finished differently from the rest.

clue.text: Tops initially borrowed during a cricket match

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the match, as if during it

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of borrowed

explanation.surface: Shirts borrowed at first during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' looks like clothing; it means the maximum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops as an informal adverb means at the very most, the idiom used for the best possible case.

clue.text: Fictional detective tracks low-class inhabitant of the underworld

indicators.note: tracks means follows, so the detective comes after the class letter

parts.note: E is the lowest social class grading in the UK
Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh police detective

explanation.surface: A detective in a novel follows a lowly criminal from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangland, fitting a detective; it is the mythical one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark realm beneath the earth and its personification, a god of darkness.

clue.text: So far, top-class war hero's entertaining 100

parts.note: U means upper-class, so top-class

indicators.note: the hero's letters hold the hundred, entertaining it

parts.note: a POW, prisoner of war, is honoured as a war hero
a ton is a hundred

explanation.surface: Until now a top war hero has scored a century.
explanation.definitionFit: So far and up to the present moment are equivalent phrases of time.

clue.text: Extremely nippy, like long-legged African resident

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of nippy

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of, like

explanation.surface: Very quick, like a leggy creature living in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa, with long legs.

clue.text: I try the ultimate in whisky, reflected one accustomed to spirits

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the last letter of whisky

explanation.surface: I'll try the last drop of whisky, thinking it over as one used to spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests drink; it is the spiritual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a master of yoga and meditation, a person at home in spiritual matters.

clue.text: Inclined to dismiss book, when reviewing Booker Prize winner

indicators.note: reviewing, seeing back, means the remaining letters are read backwards
the book letter is dismissed from the word

parts.note: being biased means inclined one way

explanation.surface: A critic minded to throw out a book while reviewing a Booker winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' looks like literary criticism; it reverses IASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize in 2006 for The Inheritance of Loss.

clue.text: Rising ballet dancer's so alive?

definitions.meaning: a dancer rising up stands ... of the feet
alert and quick to react, fully alive to things

explanation.surface: Is a ballet dancer on the up so full of life?
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick-witted is the idiom's meaning; a dancer rising is literally up on the balls of the feet.

clue.text: Type of property constructed in iron and steel

indicators.note: constructed means the letters are built into a new form

explanation.surface: A kind of building put up in iron and steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Property not used for housing, such as offices or warehouses, is commercial rather than domestic.
